To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
TM6SF2 and the MAC30/TMEM30 families are new members of the EBP sterol isomerease family, and hence are predicted to have enzymatic function.
We identified a new protein domain that is conserved among the TM6SF, EBP and MAC30 protein families.
TM6SF2 is likely to be a sterol isomeras, that MAC30/TMEM30 are likely to be also sterol isomerazses, and that the TM6SF, TMEM30 and EBP families are related by a new EXPERA domain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of new protein domains and the prediction of novel enzyme functions.
understanding the molecular function of two human genes, TM6SF2 and TMEM97 (MAC30) and the role of these genes in common metabolic diseases.
the identification of new protein domains, the analysis of their sequence conservation, and their functional characterization in the context of metabolic disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TM6SF2 and its close relatives are likely to be involved in cholesterol metabolism.
TM6SF2, TMEM97 and EBP are all enzymes that catalyze the conversion of 7-dehydrocholesterol to cholesterol, and are involved in the regulation of cholesterol metabolism.
TM6SF2, MAC30/TM6SF2 and EBP are all likely to be involved in sterol metabolism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the TM6SF and the MAC30/TMEM families are likely to be involved in sterol isomerization and that the Glu167 variant in the TMEMSF2 protein is likely to affect the catalytic function of the protein, leading to a reduction of circulating cholesterol and triglycerides and hence protection against atherosclerosis.
we have identified two new families of proteins with unknown function, TM6SF2 and TMEM97, which are likely to be involved in the metabolism of sterols.

we have identified two new enzyme homolog families, TM6SF and TMEM97, which are both involved in sterol metabolism, and that we predict that these proteins are involved in the same enzymatic process, sterol isomerization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
computational analysis of protein sequence data, when combined with experimental validation, can lead to the identification of novel protein functions and the elucidation of new disease mechanisms.
computational sequence analysis can identify new functional domains in proteins, which can then be used to predict new protein functions, and ultimately to guide experimental studies.
TM6SF2, MAC30, and EBP are all likely to be enzymes that function as sterol isomerasers.
